stories.title: Governors Island Issues RFEI for Revitalization of Former YMCA, Theater
stories.excerpt: The Trust for Gov­er­nors Island has released a Request for Expres­sions of Inter­est (RFEI) for the revi­tal­iza­tion of two his­toric build­ings on the Island, Build­ing 324 and Build­ing 330. The RFEI invites ideas from prospec­tive part­ners for the revi­tal­iza­tion of these his­toric assets, bring­ing them back into active, year-round use. The Trust seeks respons­es that pro­pose arts and cul­tur­al, recre­ation­al, or oth­er pub­lic-fac­ing uses. The two adja­cent build­ings are locat­ed with­in the Gov­er­nors Island His­toric Dis­trict. Orig­i­nal­ly con­struct­ed as a YMCA recre­ation cen­ter and a movie the­ater, respec­tive­ly, the build­ings fea­ture high ceil­ings and open floor plans. “The for­mer YMCA and Fort Jay The­ater his­tor­i­cal­ly stood as cul­tur­al anchors of Gov­er­nors Island, and we’re thrilled to present a unique oppor­tu­ni­ty to breathe new life into these icon­ic build­ings,” said Clare New­man, pres­i­dent and CEO of the Trust for Gov­er­nors Island. ​“We’re seek­ing vision­ary part­ners with bold ideas for cul­tur­al, recre­ation­al, and pub­lic-fac­ing uses that can turn untapped poten­tial into vibrant spaces for every­one to enjoy.” The com­plete RFEI can be viewed here. Submissions are due by Oct. 26. The post Governors Island Issues RFEI for Revitalization of Former YMCA, Theater appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Trust for Governors Island seeks RFEI for two historic buildings (YMCA, theater).
Submissions due Oct. 26; focus on arts, cultural, recreational, public-facing uses.
Buildings feature high ceilings, open floor plans; located in historic district.
stories.summary: The Trust for Governors Island released an RFEI for the revitalization of two historic buildings—a former YMCA recreation center and Fort Jay Theater—seeking partners with bold ideas for cultural, recreational, or public-facing uses. The adjacent buildings feature high ceilings and open floor plans. Submissions are due by October 26.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. The RFEI explicitly excludes residential use, focusing instead on arts, cultural, and recreational anchors. Governors Island's limited capacity and public-access mandate make it unsuitable for standard apartment development; any future residential component would likely be mixed-use and highly constrained by the island's master plan and nonprofit governance.

stories.title: 1031 Exchange Solutions Provider Joins Marcus & Millichap’s Preferred Partner Program
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap announced that Deferred, the first and only technology-powered qualified intermediary transforming 1031 exchanges for everyday real estate investors, has joined Marcus & Millichap’s Preferred Partner Program as a provider of 1031 exchange solutions. The relationship is designed to provide Marcus & Millichap’s clients with streamlined access to qualified intermediary services and technology-enabled 1031 exchange solutions. As interest rates, tax considerations, and market conditions continue to influence investment decisions, many commercial real estate owners seek ways to maximize after-tax proceeds while maintaining purchasing power. Through this relationship, Marcus & Millichap’s clients will gain access to Deferred’s exchange platform, educational resources, and experienced exchange professionals. “1031 exchanges remain one of the most effective tools available to investors seeking to preserve equity and reposition capital,” said Richard Matricaria, chief growth officer of Marcus & Millichap. “Deferred provides a modern, client-focused approach to guiding investors through the exchange process. Their combination of expertise, service and technology makes them a valuable addition to our Preferred Partner Program.” The post 1031 Exchange Solutions Provider Joins Marcus & Millichap’s Preferred Partner Program appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap partners with Deferred for 1031 exchange technology platform.
Move streamlines qualified intermediary access for CRE investor clients.
Addresses tax preservation and capital repositioning amid rate and market shifts.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap announced a partnership with Deferred, a technology-enabled qualified intermediary platform, to provide streamlined 1031 exchange solutions to its clients. The integration offers modern, client-focused guidance through exchanges as investors navigate interest rate, tax, and market conditions. The partnership combines Deferred's expertise, service, and technology to help investors preserve equity and reposition capital.
stories.impact: Modest indirect signal for multifamily development. Enhanced 1031 tooling reduces friction for institutional and individual CRE owners to recycle capital into new deals. This may accelerate portfolio turnover and increase acquisition competition in core markets, but the effect is primarily on capital velocity, not demand or supply fundamentals in specific multifamily markets.

stories.title: Greystone Provides $92M in Fannie Mae Loans to Metropolitan Realty
stories.excerpt: Greystone has provided a total of $91,851,000 in Fannie Mae loans to refinance and acquire three affordable housing communities located in New York. The financing was originated by senior managing director Eric Rosenstock and EVP Jeff Englund on behalf of Metropolitan Realty Group. The financing includes three affordable multifamily communities that will each undergo moderate rehabilitation as part of the transaction. Built in 1975, Pine Town Houses is a 130-unit garden-style apartment community in Long Beach, NY. Hudson View II and III, in Northern Manhattan’s Hamilton Heights neighborhood, total 129 apartments and 11 commercial spaces. Ariel Property Advisors recently arranged the Hudson View II and III acquisition. Each non-recourse, fixed-rate Fannie Mae loan features a 10-year term with five years of interest-only payments, followed by a 35-year amortization schedule. All three properties are supported by long-term Section 8 Housing Assistance Payments (HAP) contracts and are subject to long-term affordability restrictions.  The post Greystone Provides $92M in Fannie Mae Loans to Metropolitan Realty appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Greystone closes $92M Fannie Mae loans for Metropolitan Realty's three affordable properties.
Long Beach, NY (Pine Town Houses, 130 units) and Hamilton Heights, Manhattan (Hudson View II/III, 129 units + 11 commercial).
10-year fixed, 5 years IO + 35-year amort; all backed by Section 8 HAP contracts.
stories.summary: Greystone originated $91.85 million in Fannie Mae financing for Metropolitan Realty Group to refinance and acquire three affordable multifamily communities in New York: Pine Town Houses (130 units, Long Beach), and Hudson View II and III (129 units, Hamilton Heights, Manhattan). All loans feature 10-year terms with five years of interest-only payments, 35-year amortization, and are supported by long-term Section 8 Housing Assistance Payments contracts. Each property will undergo moderate rehabilitation.
stories.impact: Confirms sustained Fannie Mae appetite for stabilized, Section 8–backed affordable housing in NY metros, especially Long Island and Upper Manhattan submarkets. The 5+35 structure signals lender comfort with long-term HAP security, which de-risks value-add rehab. For developers, this underscores persistent financing availability for affordable builds targeting HAP contracts in these markets—a counter-cyclical acquisition signal when conventional multifamily lending tightens.

stories.title: E Ink Breaks Ground on Expansion of Billerica Innovation Center
stories.excerpt: E Ink, an originator, pioneer and global commercial leader in ePaper technology, broke ground on the expansion of its U.S. headquarters in Billerica, MA. The project expands the footprint at the company’s Billerica Innovation Center, which is home to 260-plus E Ink employees and serves as a key global R&D center. “Expanding our Billerica campus strengthens our ability to advance technology innovation in the United States, support our customers around the world, and contribute to the continued growth of the local economy and innovation community,” said Paul Apen, chief business and operations officer at E Ink Construction is expected to be completed by March 2027 with support from NV5 Planning & Design, Inc., IF Design L.L.C., and SPEC Process Engineering & Construction, Inc.E Ink was spun out of the MIT Media Lab in 1997 and has been headquartered in Billerica since its inception. The post E Ink Breaks Ground on Expansion of Billerica Innovation Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: E Ink breaks ground on expansion of Billerica, MA headquarters and R&D center.
Project adds to existing 260+ employee campus; completion expected March 2027.
Company spun from MIT Media Lab; HQ in Billerica since 1997.
stories.summary: E Ink broke ground on an expansion of its U.S. headquarters and innovation center in Billerica, Massachusetts, where it has housed 260+ employees and serves as a global R&D hub. Construction is expected to complete by March 2027. E Ink, a pioneer in ePaper technology, was spun out of MIT's Media Lab and has been headquartered in Billerica since its 1997 founding.
stories.impact: Positive labor-demand signal for Boston/Route 128 submarket multifamily. E Ink's R&D expansion and commitment through 2027 reinforces Billerica's tech cluster stability and supports job-growth expectations for the area. This sustained employer investment signals ongoing wage/employment resilience, which underpins rental demand in Billerica and nearby residential markets (Lexington, Burlington, Woburn). Developers should monitor for downstream hiring and wage pressure that could support rents in the immediate corridor.

stories.title: Breakthrough Properties, Tishman Speyer Provide $90M Mezz Loan for Life Science Campus
stories.excerpt: Breakthrough Properties and Tishman Speyer announced a joint investment in a $90-million mezzanine bridge loan for Aperture Del Mar, a newly constructed, 538,000-square-foot Class A life science campus in San Diego. The borrower, Gemdale USA, will use the proceeds to refinance an existing loan. The four-building lab and office campus in Del Mar Heights is fully occupied by Neurocrine Biosciences, a leading biopharmaceutical company dedicated to discovering, developing and commercializing life-changing treatments for patients with under-addressed neurological, psychiatric, endocrine and immunological disorders. Aperture Del Mar serves as Neurocrine’s mission-critical global headquarters as part of a lease that runs through 2036. The loan is part of Breakthrough’s second life science fund, which held its first close at the end of 2025. Tishman Speyer participated through its recently established debt platform. Breakthrough is a joint venture of Tishman Speyer and Bello Capital, and has several San Diego-area properties. The post Breakthrough Properties, Tishman Speyer Provide $90M Mezz Loan for Life Science Campus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Breakthrough Properties and Tishman Speyer close $90M mezzanine loan for Aperture Del Mar life science campus.
538,000 SF, four-building Class A campus in San Diego's Del Mar Heights; fully occupied by Neurocrine Biosciences.
Borrower Gemdale USA refinances existing loan; Neurocrine lease runs through 2036.
stories.summary: Breakthrough Properties and Tishman Speyer jointly provided a $90 million mezzanine bridge loan for Aperture Del Mar, a newly constructed 538,000-square-foot Class A life science campus in San Diego. The four-building campus is fully occupied by Neurocrine Biosciences under a long-term lease through 2036. Borrower Gemdale USA will use proceeds to refinance existing debt. Breakthrough's second life science fund held its first close at end of 2025.
stories.impact: Strong signal of continued capital deployment and lender confidence in San Diego life science market fundamentals. Neurocrine's 14-year remaining lease and fully-occupied status reduce refinance risk. For multifamily developers in San Diego, this confirms life science real estate remains competitively attractive to institutional capital and debt providers, which may pull investor attention and financing availability away from standard residential. However, the associated high-wage biotech employment supports rental demand in neighborhoods accessible to Del Mar and La Jolla corridors.

stories.title: West Palm Beach Multifamily Property Converted From Condos Sells for $91M
stories.excerpt: The seesaw history of a West Palm Beach residential complex has a new chapter. A joint venture between the Kamson Corporation and Joel Gluck’s Scopus Property Management has closed on a $90 million acquisition of Ponte Verde at Palm Beach Lakes, Commercial Observer has learned. The 400-unit property was built in 1990 for multifamily usage and later converted to condominiums before it was restored back to rental housing in August 2025. Prospect Ridge and Blue Owl supplied an $81 million acquisition loan for the property, which encompasses 28 acres on 1401 Village Boulevard. Previous ownership consisted of individual owners of the 400 condo units who decided to terminate the communities’ condominium association last year. Meridian Capital Group negotiated the debt with a team led by David Bollag and James Darling. “Ponte Verde is a well-located community with strong bones and a clear path forward,” Bollag said in a statement. “Rather than underwriting to where the property had been, [Prospect Ridge and Blue Owl’s] teams focused on the strength and experience of the buyer and the credibility of the business plan, which allowed us to deliver a financing solution on the timeline the transaction required.” The Ponte Verde at Palm Beach Lakes multifamily community consists of 23 two- and three-story garden-style residential buildings totaling roughly 360,488 net rentable square feet, featuring one- and two-bedroom floor plans. Community amenities include a resident clubhouse, two swimming pools, a fitness center, tennis courts, racquetball courts, a sand volleyball court, a barbecue area and spa. Prospect Ridge, Blue Owl, the Kamson Corporation and Scopus Property Management did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Kamson Corporation and Scopus Property Management acquire Ponte Verde (400 units) for $90M in West Palm Beach.
Property built 1990 (multifamily), converted to condos, restored to rental in Aug 2025; 28 acres at Village Boulevard.
Prospect Ridge and Blue Owl supplied $81M acquisition loan; Meridian Capital negotiated debt terms.
stories.summary: A joint venture between Kamson Corporation and Scopus Property Management closed a $90 million acquisition of Ponte Verde at Palm Beach Lakes, a 400-unit property in West Palm Beach built in 1990 as multifamily, converted to condominiums, and recently restored to rental housing in August 2025. The property spans 28 acres. Prospect Ridge and Blue Owl provided an $81 million acquisition loan. Meridian Capital Group negotiated the debt.
stories.impact: Signals investor appetite for condo-to-rental conversions in West Palm Beach submarket. The recent (Aug 2025) conversion and rapid institutional acquisition demonstrate strong rental demand and lender willingness to finance stabilization plays. For developers, this validates West Palm Beach as an acquisition market for under-performing condo buildings with conversion upside. The $90M valuation for a 1990-vintage, 400-unit garden-style complex suggests solid mid-market fundamentals and refinance-friendly lender appetite in South Florida.

stories.title: Waste Management Buys 146-Acre Miami-Dade Development Site for $380M
stories.excerpt: Waste Management has paid nearly $380 million for about 146 acres in Medley, Fla., where the Houston-based company will likely build another landfill, property records show. The land sits parallel to Route 27 at 9515 Northwest 95th Avenue near the Everglades national park. About half the site remains vacant while the rest serves as a surface truck parking lot. The property sits adjacent to Waste Management’s 170-acre Medley Landfill complex. An entity tied to Hialeah Gardens-based Lowell Dunn Company sold the land. The same entity provided $366.8 million in seller financing, which is scheduled to mature in 2046. In a recorded easement, Lowell Dunn Company also agreed to allow Waste Management to install underground stormwater pipes across its neighboring property, enabling runoff from Waste Management’s site to discharge into a canal north of the property. Representatives for the buyer and seller did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The deal marks the second acquisition made by a waste management company in Miami-Dade County just this month. Woodlands, Texas-based Waste Connections paid $51 million for a 12-acre surface trucking parking lot in Miami Gardens. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Waste Management acquires 146 acres in Medley, FL (near Route 27) for ~$380M.
Land adjacent to WM's 170-acre Medley Landfill complex; seller financing $366.8M through 2046.
Half-vacant site plus truck parking lot; industrial/infrastructure use, not residential.
stories.summary: Waste Management purchased approximately 146 acres in Medley, Florida for nearly $380 million, intending to develop a landfill adjacent to its existing 170-acre Medley Landfill complex. The seller, Lowell Dunn Company, provided $366.8 million in seller financing maturing in 2046. The site, located near Route 27 and the Everglades, is currently half-vacant and used partly as a truck parking lot.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. This is large-scale industrial/waste infrastructure acquisition in a peripheral Miami-Dade corridor (near Everglades). The deal reinforces Medley's role as an industrial logistics and waste-management hub, which may limit nearby residential demand and increase environmental/industrial perception risk for adjacent multifamily sites. Developers should note Medley's continued industrial zoning and infrastructure focus; it remains unsuitable for class-A residential targeting.

stories.title: Carlyle Group, Haussmann Submit Plans for 99 Units at Brooklyn’s 566 Grand Avenue
stories.excerpt: Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development have plans to partner on a 99-unit apartment complex in Brooklyn’s Crown Heights neighborhood. The two developers filed plans Thursday with the New York City Department of Buildings (DOB) to bring a new 12-story mixed-use building to 566 Grand Avenue, near the corner of Grand Avenue and Bergen Street. Spokespeople for Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. If approved, the building will feature 99 Class A apartments, according to the filing, as well as ground-floor retail space. There will be 10 apartments on the second floor, 11 units each on the third through ninth floors, and four apartments each on floors 10, 11 and 12. The developers also plan to include several in-demand amenities at the property, such as a pet spa, a tenant theater, a game room, a children’s playroom, coworking space, a gym and an outdoor lounge. It is unclear if Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development plan to utilize the 485-x tax abatement program, which offers developers significant and lengthy tax breaks if their buildings feature a certain percentage of affordable housing. However, the 99-unit plan does provide a clue that this might be the case. A widely unpopular component of the 485-x program is higher construction wage requirements for buildings with 100 or more units. However, buildings with 99 or fewer units that utilize this program are not bound by those wage requirements. Crown Heights has been awash with residential building plans as of late. Avery Hall is planning an 18-story, 250-unit development at 1550 Bedford Avenue, while the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) is looking to build a 300-unit housing development in the neighborhood at 1119 Pacific Street. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development file plans for 99-unit apartment building at 566 Grand Avenue, Brooklyn.
12-story mixed-use (Class A residential + ground-floor retail) in Crown Heights near Bergen Street.
Building includes pet spa, theater, game room, coworking, gym, and amenities; second floor 10 units, floors 3–9 with 11 units each.
stories.summary: Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development filed plans with NYC Department of Buildings for a 12-story, 99-unit Class A apartment complex at 566 Grand Avenue in Crown Heights, Brooklyn. The building will include ground-floor retail and in-demand amenities: pet spa, tenant theater, game room, children's playroom, coworking, gym, and outdoor lounge. Unit distribution includes 10 on the second floor, 11 each on floors 3–9, and four each on floors 10–12.
stories.impact: Continued Brooklyn multifamily pipeline activity by institutional sponsors (Carlyle, Haussmann) in Crown Heights submarket signals sustained development appetite despite macro headwinds. The emphasis on Class A units and premium amenities targets younger, higher-income renters. For developers, this indicates Crown Heights remains competitive for new supply; timing of approvals and construction feasibility will depend on construction costs, labor availability, and financing terms in 2026–2027. Tax abatement (485-x) remains a possible competitive advantage that developers should actively pursue.

stories.title: Lightstone Capital Refis San Diego Apartments With $34M Loan

Lightstone Capital originated the senior loan for Svitak’s Kaya Apartments development in San Diego’s Bankers Hill neighborhood. John Zubak, managing director and head of origination, western region at Lightstone Capital, originated the deal. “From the outset, Kaya has been about creating housing that is deeply connected to the character of Bankers Hill while fostering a true sense of community,” Svitak said in a statement. Located at 2700 Third Avenue, Kaya Apartments debuted last year with 78 units ranging from studios to two bedrooms. Community amenities at the fully-leased complex include coworking space, community lounge, a shared kitchen and on-site café. Lightstone Capital also closed a $23.4 million senior bridge loan in July for Alliance Development Services‘ The Flats at TerraMar multifamily project in Carlsbad, Calif. Located at 5010 Avenida Encinas 32 miles north of San Diego, the 98-unit apartment community with 15 designated as affordable housing will involve converting a former Studio 6 hotel. bullets: Lightstone Capital closes $34.25M senior bridge loan for Kaya Apartments in San Diego's Bankers Hill.
78-unit newly completed project (studios to two-bedroom); fully leased; includes coworking, lounge, shared kitchen, café.
Developer Jeff Svitak; located 2700 Third Avenue; part of broader San Diego multifamily refinancing activity.
stories.summary: Lightstone Capital originated a $34.25 million senior bridge loan for Kaya Apartments, a newly completed 78-unit multifamily project in San Diego's Bankers Hill neighborhood. The fully-leased development features studios to two-bedroom units and amenities including coworking space, community lounge, shared kitchen, and on-site café. Developer Jeff Svitak is repositioning the asset through bridge financing. Lightstone also closed a $23.4 million senior bridge loan in July for another San Diego-area multifamily project (The Flats at TerraMar).
stories.impact: Demonstrates active bridge-lending market in San Diego multifamily, particularly for newly stabilized, fully-leased assets in in-fill submarkets like Bankers Hill. Lightstone's willingness to finance two separate projects (78 and 98 units) in recent months signals lender confidence in San Diego rental fundamentals and exit liquidity. For developers, this underscores San Diego's ongoing attractiveness for value-add/new-build multifamily and the availability of structured debt in the 25–35M range for stabilized products.

stories.title: Rexford Plans Up to $2B in Sales After Posting $507M Loss in Q2
stories.excerpt: Rexford Industrial Realty is dramatically accelerating its shift from being the most aggressive industrial buyer in Southern California into perhaps the region’s biggest seller. The Los Angeles-based real estate investment trust (REIT) has identified about $2 billion of “noncore assets” for disposition as it continues to prioritize keeping tenants in Rexford buildings. That property sales forecast is sharply up from the previous range of $400 million to $500 million. During the REIT’s earnings call Friday, CEO Laura Clark said the disposition pool encompasses about 8 million square feet with limited value-creation potential, shorter lease terms, and rents substantially above market — generally by more than 20 percent. Chief Financial Officer Michael Fitzmaurice said about $1 billion will repay debt maturing in 2027, rather than refinance into a higher rate environment. The remaining proceeds will be guided by market conditions. “We’re not de-levering to sit idle; we’re de-levering to redeploy,” Fitzmaurice said. The vast majority of Rexford’s property sales are expected to close before the end of the year. “We expect that pricing will be achieved at levels that allow us to redeploy proceeds on a neutral to accretive basis through our 2027 FFO per share, and this is not a dilutive exercise,” Clark said. Rexford said it sold seven properties totaling approximately 572,000 square feet for $137.9 million during the second quarter, after disposing of five properties for $127.4 million in the first quarter. The company previously known for 10-figure buying sprees has completed no acquisitions this year. Rexford plans to use property sales proceeds to repay debt, repurchase shares and pursue higher-yielding investments. It bought back $100 million of stock during the quarter, bringing its 2026 repurchases to $300 million, and its board subsequently authorized a new $1 billion repurchase program. bullets: Rexford Industrial forecasts $2B asset sales (up from $400–500M prior guidance); ~8M SF of noncore assets.
Portfolio targets rents 20%+ above market; shorter lease terms; Q2 loss $507M includes unrealized mark-downs.
CFO Fitzmaurice: $1B repays 2027 debt maturities; balance to redeploy based on market conditions.
stories.summary: Rexford Industrial Realty is accelerating portfolio dispositions, forecasting approximately $2 billion in sales of 'noncore assets'—roughly 8 million square feet—with rents substantially above market (generally 20%+ above) and limited value-creation potential. About $1 billion of proceeds will repay debt maturing in 2027; the remainder will be redeployed per market conditions. The REIT posted a $507 million loss in Q2, reflecting unrealized mark-downs on its industrial portfolio as Southern California cap rates have expanded.
stories.impact: Indirect supply-side signal for Southern California. Rexford's shift from acquisition to disposition mode suggests an over-heated industrial market in the early 2020s, with subsequent cap-rate expansion and rental-rate normalization diminishing previously high-conviction assets. While this does not directly affect multifamily supply, the repricing of SoCal real estate and capital reallocation away from industrial may increase competitive pressure for institutional investment capital and debt into multifamily. Developers should monitor Rexford's disposition timeline and pricing trends to gauge broader SoCal CRE sentiment and refinance risk in 2027 when broader debt maturities peak.
